passage:
Every Friday, Mr. White asked his students three questions: What did you learn What was difficult Who helped you
Students wrote answers on small cards. They did not need to put their names on them.
At first, the answers were short. Later, students became more honest. They wrote about confusing lessons, helpful friends, and times they were proud.
Mr. White read the cards over the weekend and changed his teaching when many students had the same problem.
The third question became the most important. Students began to notice help they had received.
Learning was no longer only about correct answers. It was also about understanding effort, difficulty, and the people who made the week easier.
